metadata.title: Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction by Locally Linear Embedding
metadata.authors: Sam T. Roweis and Lawrence K. Saul
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: Title and authors match registry expectation (Roweis & Saul, LLE, Science 290:2323-2326, 2000).

nodes.name: Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction Problem
nodes.statement: Given $N$ high-dimensional inputs $\vec{X}_i \in \mathbb{R}^D$ sampled from an underlying $d$-dimensional manifold ($d \ll D$), discover low-dimensional coordinates $\vec{Y}_i \in \mathbb{R}^d$ that map the data into a single global coordinate system while preserving neighborhood structure.
nodes.statement_clean: Map high-dimensional data lying on a low-dimensional manifold into a single global low-dimensional coordinate system that preserves neighborhood relations.

nodes.name: Neighborhood of a Data Point
nodes.statement: For each data point $\vec{X}_i$, a set of neighbors is assigned, e.g. by choosing the $K$ nearest neighbors in Euclidean distance, by taking all points within a ball of fixed radius, or by using prior knowledge.
nodes.statement_clean: A neighborhood of $\vec{X}_i$ is a small set of nearby data points (commonly the $K$ nearest neighbors).

nodes.name: Reconstruction Weights $W_{ij}$
nodes.statement: The weights $W_{ij}$ summarize the contribution of the $j$-th data point to the linear reconstruction of $\vec{X}_i$ from its neighbors, with $W_{ij}=0$ when $\vec{X}_j$ is not a neighbor of $\vec{X}_i$ and $\sum_j W_{ij}=1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Linear coefficients that reconstruct each point from its neighbors, supported on the neighborhood and summing to one across $j$.

nodes.name: Embedding Vectors $\vec{Y}_i$
nodes.statement: Each high-dimensional input $\vec{X}_i$ is mapped to a low-dimensional vector $\vec{Y}_i \in \mathbb{R}^d$ representing global internal coordinates on the manifold.
nodes.statement_clean: Low-dimensional coordinate vector assigned to each input by LLE.

nodes.name: Symmetric Matrix $M$
nodes.statement: The sparse symmetric $N \times N$ matrix $M_{ij} = \delta_{ij} - W_{ij} - W_{ji} + \sum_k W_{ki} W_{kj}$, equal to $(I-W)^T(I-W)$, whose bottom $d+1$ eigenvectors yield the LLE embedding.
nodes.statement_clean: The matrix $(I-W)^T(I-W)$ whose bottom eigenvectors give the embedding.

nodes.name: Reconstruction Cost $\varepsilon(W)$
nodes.statement: $\varepsilon(W) = \sum_i \big| \vec{X}_i - \sum_j W_{ij} \vec{X}_j \big|^2$, the sum of squared distances between data points and their reconstructions from neighbors.
nodes.statement_clean: Cost summing squared reconstruction errors of each $\vec{X}_i$ from its neighbors with weights $W_{ij}$.

nodes.name: Embedding Cost $\Phi(Y)$
nodes.statement: $\Phi(Y) = \sum_i \big| \vec{Y}_i - \sum_j W_{ij} \vec{Y}_j \big|^2$, the locally linear reconstruction error in the embedding space, with weights $W_{ij}$ fixed and coordinates $\vec{Y}_i$ optimized.
nodes.statement_clean: Cost penalizing failure of the embedded points to be reconstructed by the same weights $W_{ij}$.

nodes.name: Cost Matrix $M_{ij}$
nodes.statement: $M_{ij} = \delta_{ij} - W_{ij} - W_{ji} + \sum_k W_{ki} W_{kj}$, so that $\Phi(Y) = \sum_{ij} M_{ij}\,(\vec{Y}_i \cdot \vec{Y}_j)$.

nodes.name: Well-Sampled Locally Linear Manifold
nodes.statement: The data $\vec{X}_i$ are sampled densely enough from an underlying smooth $d$-dimensional manifold ($d \ll D$) so that each point and its neighbors lie on or close to a locally linear patch.
nodes.statement_clean: The data densely sample a smooth low-dimensional manifold so that local neighborhoods are approximately linear.

nodes.name: Embedding Constraints (Well-Posedness)
nodes.statement: Embedding coordinates are centered, $\sum_i \vec{Y}_i = \vec{0}$, and have unit covariance, $\frac{1}{N}\sum_i \vec{Y}_i \vec{Y}_i^{\top} = I_d$, removing translational and rescaling degeneracies.
nodes.statement_clean: Embeddings are constrained to be centered with unit covariance to make the eigenproblem well-posed.

nodes.name: Symmetry of Reconstruction Weights
nodes.statement: The constrained optimal weights $W_{ij}$ minimizing $\varepsilon(W)$ subject to support on neighbors and $\sum_j W_{ij}=1$ are invariant under rotations, rescalings, and translations of $\vec{X}_i$ together with its neighbors.
nodes.statement_clean: Optimal LLE weights are invariant to rigid-similarity transformations of any neighborhood.
conclusions: $W_{ij}$ is invariant under rotations, rescalings, and translations of $\vec{X}_i$ and its neighbors
Translation invariance follows specifically from the sum-to-one constraint

nodes.name: Transferability of Local Weights to Manifold Coordinates
nodes.statement: If a neighborhood of $\vec{X}_i$ is mapped to internal manifold coordinates by a translation, rotation, and rescaling, then the same weights $W_{ij}$ that reconstruct $\vec{X}_i$ in $D$ dimensions also reconstruct its embedded coordinates $\vec{Y}_i$ in $d$ dimensions.
nodes.statement_clean: Because the optimal weights are invariant to local similarity transforms, they transfer from data space to the manifold's intrinsic coordinates.
assumptions: $\vec{X}_i$ lies on or near a smooth $d$-dimensional manifold with $d \ll D$
There exists a linear (translation+rotation+rescaling) mapping from the neighborhood to internal coordinates

nodes.name: Closed-Form Optimal Weights
nodes.statement: For a single point $\vec{x}$ with neighbors $\vec{\eta}_j$, the constrained weights minimizing $|\vec{x}-\sum_{j=1}^{K} w_j \vec{\eta}_j|^2$ subject to $\sum_j w_j=1$ are given in closed form by $w_j = \sum_k C^{-1}_{jk}(\vec{x}\cdot\vec{\eta}_k + \lambda)$, where $C_{jk}=\vec{\eta}_j\cdot\vec{\eta}_k$ and $\lambda$ is the Lagrange multiplier enforcing the sum-to-one constraint.
nodes.statement_clean: The constrained least-squares reconstruction weights have a closed-form solution via the inverse Gram matrix and a Lagrange multiplier.
assumptions: Correlation matrix $C$ invertible (or conditioned by $C \leftarrow C + \epsilon I$ if near-singular)
nodes.notes: PDF math partially garbled; reconstructed from notes 7 and 9 in source.

nodes.name: Eigenvector Solution of the Embedding
nodes.statement: Subject to the centering and unit-covariance constraints, the optimal embedding minimizing $\Phi(Y)$ is given (up to global rotation) by the bottom $d+1$ eigenvectors of $M = (I-W)^T(I-W)$; the very bottom eigenvector (the all-ones translation mode of eigenvalue zero) is discarded, and the remaining $d$ eigenvectors are the LLE coordinates.
nodes.statement_clean: The embedding solving Eq. 2 is the bottom $d$ nontrivial eigenvectors of $(I-W)^T(I-W)$.
conclusions: Optimal $\vec{Y}_i$ are the bottom $d+1$ eigenvectors of $M$, discarding the all-ones zero mode
Solution is unique up to a global rotation

nodes.name: Locally Linear Embedding (LLE)
nodes.statement: Three-step unsupervised algorithm that computes neighborhood-preserving low-dimensional embeddings of high-dimensional data by fitting local linear reconstructions and then solving a sparse eigenvalue problem.
nodes.statement_clean: Unsupervised three-step embedding: (1) find neighbors, (2) fit reconstruction weights, (3) compute embedding by sparse eigendecomposition.
nodes.pseudocode: 1. For each i, assign K nearest neighbors of X_i. 2. Compute weights W_{ij} minimizing eps(W) = sum_i |X_i - sum_j W_{ij} X_j|^2 with W_{ij}=0 for non-neighbors and sum_j W_{ij}=1 (closed-form per note 7). 3. Compute Y_i minimizing Phi(Y) = sum_i |Y_i - sum_j W_{ij} Y_j|^2 by computing the bottom d+1 eigenvectors of M = (I-W)^T(I-W); discard the trivial all-ones eigenvector; the remaining d eigenvectors are the embedding coordinates.

nodes.name: Assign Neighbors
nodes.statement: For each data point $\vec{X}_i$, identify its $K$ nearest neighbors (e.g. by Euclidean distance or normalized dot products), or alternatively all points within a fixed-radius ball, or a neighbor set chosen from prior knowledge.

nodes.name: Compute Reconstruction Weights $W_{ij}$
nodes.statement: Compute weights $W_{ij}$ that best linearly reconstruct $\vec{X}_i$ from its neighbors by solving the constrained least-squares problem of Eq. 1 (closed form via the local Gram matrix $C_{jk}=\vec{\eta}_j\cdot\vec{\eta}_k$ and a Lagrange multiplier enforcing $\sum_j W_{ij}=1$).

nodes.name: Compute Embedding Vectors $\vec{Y}_i$
nodes.statement: Compute low-dimensional embedding vectors $\vec{Y}_i$ best reconstructed by $W_{ij}$ by minimizing $\Phi(Y)$ in Eq. 2 via the bottom $d+1$ eigenvectors of the sparse symmetric matrix $M = (I-W)^T(I-W)$ in Eq. 3, discarding the trivial all-ones eigenvector.

nodes.name: Synthetic 2D-Manifold-in-3D
nodes.statement: $N=2000$ data points sampled from a two-dimensional manifold embedded in $\mathbb{R}^3$ (the manifold introduced by Tenenbaum); LLE with $K=20$ Euclidean nearest neighbors recovers the global 2D structure with neighborhood-preserving color coding.
nodes.statement_clean: On 2000 points from Tenenbaum's 2D-in-3D manifold, LLE with K=20 recovers the underlying 2D coordinates.

nodes.name: Face Images Embedding
nodes.statement: $N=2000$ photographs of a single face digitized as $20\times 28$ grayscale images ($D=560$) are embedded by LLE with $K=12$ Euclidean nearest neighbors; the first two LLE coordinates organize faces by pose and expression.
nodes.statement_clean: LLE applied to 2000 face images (D=560, K=12) yields a 2D embedding organized by pose and expression.

nodes.name: Word-Document Embedding
nodes.statement: Word-document counts for $N=5000$ words across $D=31{,}000$ articles in Grolier's Encyclopedia; LLE with $K=20$ neighbors (similarity by normalized dot products of count vectors) yields an embedding in which words with similar contexts are co-located in a continuous semantic space.
nodes.statement_clean: LLE applied to 5000 word-document count vectors (D=31000, K=20, dot-product neighbors) produces a semantic embedding co-locating words used in similar contexts.

nodes.name: Single Free Parameter $K$
nodes.statement: Once neighbors are chosen, the optimal weights $W_{ij}$ and coordinates $\vec{Y}_i$ are computed by standard linear-algebra methods, so the algorithm has only one free parameter: the number of neighbors $K$.

nodes.name: Global Optima and No Local Minima
nodes.statement: A single pass through the three steps finds global minima of the reconstruction and embedding costs in Eqs. 1 and 2; LLE's optimizations do not involve local minima, in contrast to autoencoders, self-organizing maps, and latent-variable models.

nodes.name: Sparsity and Computational Savings
nodes.statement: The matrix $M$ can be stored and manipulated as the sparse product $(I-W)^T(I-W)$, and its bottom $d+1$ eigenvectors can be found efficiently without a full diagonalization, giving substantial savings for large $N$.

nodes.name: Maximum Recoverable Embedding Dimension
nodes.statement: For a fixed number of neighbors $K$, the maximum number of embedding dimensions LLE can be expected to recover is strictly less than $K$.

nodes.name: Conditioning of $C$
nodes.statement: If the local correlation matrix $C$ is nearly singular, it can be conditioned before inversion by adding a small multiple of the identity, $C \leftarrow C + \epsilon I$, which penalizes large weights that exploit correlations beyond the sampling precision.

nodes.name: Incremental Embedding Dimensions
nodes.statement: LLE scales well with $d$ and does not require gridding the embedding space; adding more dimensions does not change the existing ones, so LLE need not be rerun to obtain higher-dimensional embeddings.

nodes.name: Disjoint Manifolds via Connected Components
nodes.statement: LLE can be formulated for data lying on several disjoint manifolds: form the neighborhood graph, detect its connected components by examining powers of the adjacency matrix, and analyze each component separately, since different components decouple in the LLE eigenproblem.

nodes.name: Online LLE for Time-Ordered Data
nodes.statement: If neighbors correspond to nearby observations in time, the reconstruction weights can be computed online and the embedding can be obtained by diagonalizing a sparse banded matrix.

nodes.name: Isomap (cited)
nodes.statement: Nonlinear dimensionality reduction algorithm that estimates pairwise geodesic distances between data points along shortest paths through the neighborhood graph and then applies MDS to recover an embedding preserving these distances.

nodes.name: Principal Component Analysis (cited)
nodes.statement: Linear dimensionality reduction by projecting data onto the top eigenvectors of the input covariance matrix.

nodes.name: Multidimensional Scaling (cited)
nodes.statement: Classical embedding method that computes low-dimensional coordinates preserving pairwise (Euclidean or generalized) distances between data points.
